title: "Sample Questions 01"
output:
  pdf_document: default
  html_document: default
---

Consider the following probability density function (pdf) over the support 
$(0,1)$:

\begin{equation*}
f(x) = 
\begin{cases}
4x^3 & \text{if } 0 < x < 1 \\
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\end{equation*}

```{r echo=FALSE}
rf <- function(n) {
  U <- runif(n)
  X <- U^(1/4)
  X
}
```

1.  Write a function called `rf`, that generates i.i.d observations from this pdf.
    It should take in exactly one argument, $n$, that determines how many random
    variates to return. For instance:

```{r}
set.seed(33)
rf(n = 5)
```

2.  Now generate 10,000 random variates from this pdf and store them in a vector 
    named `X`.
    
3.  Use base R to re-create the following plot of the pdf over the interval (0,1). It 
    overlays the density on the histogram of generated values.

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.align='center', out.width='75%'}
X <- rf(1e4)
x <- seq(0, 1, length.out=100)
y <- 4*x^3
hist(X, freq=FALSE, main="Histogram and pdf")
lines(x, y, col="red", type="l", main="Plot of pdf f(x)", lwd=2)
```


Your script must generate: 

- a function named `rf`,
- a vector named `X`, and 
- the above plot.
